fixes.explanation: True. The text says they prompted some men to say, and those men say, "We heard Stephen speak words of blasphemy against Moses and against God." So the men from the synagogue get others to say it. Blasphemy means speaking against God, which is a heavy thing to say about a man.

It's true, baker. The text says they prompted some men to say, and those men say, "We heard Stephen speak words of blasphemy against Moses and against God." The men from the synagogue are the ones prompting. The charge is a heavy one, and it comes right after the debate.

Sacrifices? Not one mention, friend. The Twelve say, "It is unacceptable for us to neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables." The word of God is the thing they refuse to drop. Tables are one job, and the word is another.
Seven it is! The Twelve say, "…select from among you seven men confirmed to be full of the Spirit and wisdom." Later in verse 5 the group chooses seven names, so the number holds all the way through.
Fasting isn't in their plan. The Twelve say they "…will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word." Prayer is the missing piece.
Healing, friend? Not in this plan. The Twelve say they "…will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word." Prayer is the partner of the word here, and that's the pick.
Silas, a leader among the brothers (Acts 15:22), isn't named in this passage. Verse 5 says the man "…full of faith and of the Holy Spirit…" is Stephen. Silas has to wait for another passage.
No king shows up here, friend. The people, elders and scribes get stirred up, and then Stephen is seized. Verse 12 says they brought him "…before the Sanhedrin…" which is Israel's ruling council.

Neither priests nor sacrifices get a mention in the charge, friend. Verse 13 gives it: "This man never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law." Those witnesses are called false, so the charge itself isn't true.

The text doesn't say that. Verse 15 says, "…they saw that his face was like the face of an angel." He's standing in front of the Sanhedrin with false witnesses against him. What they see is a face like the face of an angel.

Anger isn't what they see. Verse 15 says, "…they saw that his face was like the face of an angel." All who were sitting in the Sanhedrin looked at him intently. What they saw was a face like an angel's.
